extracted.intended_audience: research administrators and investigators preparing NIH G11 (PAR-18-335) capacity-building grant applications, especially at LMIC institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH G11 capacity-building (Global Infectious Disease Research Administration Development Award) grant application, including required forms, project narrative, biosketches, facilities descriptions, human/animal protections, training plans, timeline, and sustainability elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Eligibility Constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical Trial: Not Allowed (FOA: PAR-18-335).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposed project does not propose or include a clinical trial; follow the FOA limitation exactly when designing aims and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Funding Opportunity Instructions / Application Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FOA-specific formats and limits; refer to NIAID sample applications and the FOA for current rules and formatting requirements (link provided). Sample content may be outdated—confirm against current FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF-424 (R&R) Required Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full SF 424 (R&R) information: type of submission, applicant legal name and contact info, PD/PI contact, authorized representative signature, start/end dates, applicant type, and related identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate all mandatory fields (applicant DUNS, EIN/TIN, organization info, project title, congressional district, etc.) and ensure authorized representative signs and dates; follow OMB form instructions and expiration dates shown on forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract (file)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise Project Summary/Abstract (file listed as Projectsummary_CaBERa-II_NOA_2019.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize rationale, objectives, and expected impact; include public-health significance and succinctly state the project scope and approach as required by FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (file)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Narrative describing public-health relevance (file listed ProjectNarrative_CaBERA-II_NOA_2019.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed work will benefit public health; keep it explicit and linked to the FOA’s mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents / Required Attachment List
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all required application components (Table of Contents shows required items: Performance Sites; Research & Related Other Project Information; Project Summary; Project Narrative; Facilities & Other Resources; Senior/Key Person; Budget; Budget Justification; Research Plan; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Human Subjects info; Bibliography; Letters of Support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble attachments in the FOA-specified order and include each listed component; use correct file names and ensure all referenced attachments are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional facilities, equipment, networks, power/water backup, biosafety, administrative units (e.g., Office of Research Support), and scientific departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate capacity to support the project: list relevant departments, staffing levels, computing/network resources, biostatistics support, ORS structure, and contingency resources (generators, solar, water). Use concrete details to show capability to execute and sustain activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Involvement and Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether human subjects are involved; if YES, specify exemption status, exemption number or IRB review pending/approved, IRB approval date, and Human Subject Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, provide full human subjects sections per PHS forms, including protections, consent, and monitoring; if no human subjects, explicitly mark 'No'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals Use and Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are used; if YES, provide IACUC review status, IACUC approval date, and Animal Welfare Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If animals are used, include welfare assurances and describe justification and procedures; if no animals, explicitly mark 'No'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary/Privileged Information Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether proprietary/privileged information is included in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark yes/no and, if yes, follow FOA/agency rules for protecting confidential information and expect redactions under FOIA when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Impact Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the project has an actual or potential impact on the environment and whether an exemption, environmental assessment (EA), or environmental impact statement (EIS) has been performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If environmental impacts exist, provide required documentation and explanations; follow agency environmental review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Activities / Activities Outside the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare if project involves activities outside the United States or partnerships with international collaborators and identify countries (e.g., Ghana).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide optional explanation of roles of international partners and ensure compliance with FOA requirements for foreign components and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear Specific Aims that state the overarching objective and discrete aims (e.g., establish research management offices, train staff, serve as resource hub).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write focused, measurable aims aligned with the FOA’s goals; NIH reviewers evaluate the clarity and importance of Specific Aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy / Approach (including Innovation & Significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe Significance (why the work matters), Innovation (novel aspects), and Approach (methods/activities) including rationale and prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NIH triad: justify importance (Significance), articulate novelty (Innovation), and present a feasible, detailed Approach including timelines, expected outcomes, and evaluation. For capacity-building, document institutional context and evidence that approach will result in sustained capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Training Plan and Capacity Building Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concrete staff training plan: e.g., shadowing at Yale OSP for two weeks, needs assessments, customized training modules, development of grants management manuals, and mentoring-to-trainer cascade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail who will be trained, duration, curricula, milestones (three 6-month periods: needs assessment/registrations; manuals/SOPs/customized training; dissemination and grant submissions), and how training will build sustainable institutional capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and Milestones (18-month timeline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline of activities across the project period (first six months, next six months, last six months) with concrete tasks: needs assessment, registrations (DUNS, SAM, eRA Commons, Grants.gov), job descriptions, recruitment, training, dissemination, and proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear timeline table or Gantt-like plan with deliverables tied to project periods; include timing for registrations which may take weeks and plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected Outcomes and Measurable Deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerate expected outcomes: institutionalization of research management, training and capacity building, restructuring of offices, advocacy services, increased grant submissions and research portfolio, established accountability/reporting, notification processes for funding opportunities, and links with external agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define measurable indicators (e.g., number of offices established, number of staff trained, number of competitive grants submitted) and include evaluation/monitoring plans to demonstrate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how activities will be sustained post-award: recruit permanent Research Administrator positions, periodic trainings, design programs/activities to attract donors, and build institutional policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain financial and operational sustainability steps (e.g., hiring, revenue-generating programs, institutional policy adoption) and how trainees will become trainers to maintain capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch Requirements for Senior/Key Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide biographical sketches for senior/key personnel following the specified format; 'DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.' Include Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Contribution to Science, Education/Training, and Attachments for Current & Pending Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed biosketch template exactly, adhere to the five-page limit, and include relevant past contributions, roles on prior grants, and ongoing/completed support to demonstrate capability and avoid overlap-of-effort concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current & Pending Support / Past and Ongoing Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: List ongoing and completed research support for key personnel to demonstrate relevant experience and potential conflicts/overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include grant numbers, roles, project goals, and dates; ensure transparency about commitments and show how new project fits with existing support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Administrative Support and ORS Function
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional administrative resources, ORS staffing, roles (research development officer, finance officers, database officer), and coordination for grants management and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show evidence of institutional commitment (staff, offices, reporting lines, administrative capacity) and describe how ORS will manage pre- and post-award processes, financial management, effort reporting, and subawards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and Compliance Requirements for Institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete necessary institutional registrations: DUNS, NCAGE, eRA Commons, SAM, Grants.gov, and other funder-specific registrations (DANIDA, EDCTP, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for registration timelines (registrations may take weeks); complete registrations early in the first six-month period as part of needs assessment/initial activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Research & Related Budget, Cumulative Budget, and Budget Justification supporting personnel, training visits, workshops, manuals, and other project costs (Budget Justification file referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail direct costs and rationales, show how funds support aims and sustainability, and ensure indirect costs and consortium F&A are handled per FOA rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support and Institutional Commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Letters of Support and evidence of institutional commitment (listed in Table of Contents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide letters from partner institutions and collaborators that commit resources or describe roles; tie letters to workplan and demonstrate partner buy-in.
